title: England captain Ben Stokes admits he must work in ‘a different way’ with Brendon McCullum
content:
Ben Stokes has admitted he will have to work in “a different way” with Brendon McCullum as England look to rebuild reputations shattered by their Ashes humiliation.

The England captain moved to quell speculation that he and the coach are not aligned anymore after seemingly moving in contrasting directions during the 4-1 defeat by Australia.

But Stokes, in a carefully controlled interview with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB), has accepted that the Bazball style he appeared to abandon during the Ashes “might just look a little bit different’’ when England begin their Test summer against New Zealand in June.

“When you’re in a position of leadership along with someone else, if anyone thinks you’re always going to agree on everything then it’s just impossible,” said Stokes in the ECB interview released on Tuesday. “You need debate. You need discussions.

“As similar as me and Brendon (McCullum) are, we’re also dissimilar in other areas. The thing we both want is to be as successful as we possibly can be, but how we get to being successful might be the same here, but slightly differs there.

“I’m very confident in mine and Brendon’s ability to be able to work together because we’ve done it for such a long period of time now. But work together in a slightly different way. The main point of me and Brendon is making this team as good as they can be, but it might just look a bit different now to how that operates.”

The pairing of Stokes and McCullum appeared a masterstroke when managing director Rob Key put them together in 2022, and they initially transformed in exciting style a team that had won just one of their previous 17 Tests under captain Joe Root and coach Chris Silverwood.

But the ultra-positive Bazball methods began to unravel the better the opposition England faced, and they have yet to defeat either Australia or India in four five-Test series.

The captain appeared to have lost faith when he began moving away from the Bazball messaging during the Ashes, saying his dressing room was “no place for weak men” and batting with particular defensive care on the flattest pitch of the series in Adelaide.

That led to the questioning of the relationship between the pair, but Stokes is adamant he and McCullum are still close. And his comments suggest it is McCullum who will have to compromise, as the ECB said he would when they backed him in an Ashes review.

“With what me and Brendon were able to achieve over a four-year period I just couldn’t imagine doing what we were trying to do with anyone else,” adds Stokes. “We’re both proud men in what we do. We put a lot of heart and soul into this job.

“Saying we weren’t aligned I think is a massive overstatement and hopefully we’ll still be together at the end of 2027, winning what we want to win.”
